body:
Labels in Godot always have their drop shadow renders behind the outlines. However, this image from the proposal raises the question: What do we do with the stackable effects?

Also, the way this feature is implemented involves two additions to the current theme system. Are there better alternatives?

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/486d3d54-3eb7-49ce-8375-ee0062efd85e)
I did not handle the new enum types in `doc_tools`, but the current commit should compile if using simple scons command (`scons dev_build=yes`).

I choose not to implement stacked drop shadows (and its outlines) for now, as it's adding even more complexity to the render loop. The draw loop looks like this after this PR:

Edited: I have modified the Label's render code, and implement the drop shadow on top of the modification.

```
Paragraphs Loop
│
├─ Check if paragraph needs rendering
│  │
│  └─ Lines Loop (for each visible line)
│     │
│     ├─ Setup line metrics (ascent, descent, glyphs)
│     │
│     ├─ Drawing Steps Loop
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_SHADOW_OUTLINE
│     │  │  └─ Skip if font_shadow_color.a == 0 || shadow_outline_size <= 0
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_SHADOW
│     │  │  └─ Skip if font_shadow_color.a == 0
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_STACKED_OUTLINE
│     │  │  └─ Skip if font_stacked_outline_colors/sizes empty
│     │  │  └─ Multiple iterations based on outline stack depth
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_OUTLINE
│     │  │  └─ Skip if outline_size <= 0 || font_outline_color.a == 0
│     │  │
│     │  └─ DRAW_STEP_TEXT
│     │
│     └─ For each drawing step:
│        │
│        ├─ Draw RTL ellipsis (if RTL and has ellipsis)
│        │
│        ├─ Draw main text glyphs (respecting trim positions)
│        │
│        └─ Draw LTR ellipsis (if LTR and has ellipsis)
│
└─ Move to next paragraph
```

If we are implementing stacked shadow and its outlines, we will end up have the following:

```
Paragraphs Loop
│
├─ Check if paragraph needs rendering
│  │
│  └─ Lines Loop (for each visible line)
│     │
│     ├─ Setup line metrics (ascent, descent, glyphs)
│     │
│     ├─ Drawing Steps Loop
      │  │
[+]   │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_STACKED_SHADOW_AND_OUTLINE
[+]   │  │  └─ Multiple iterations that draw shadow outline and shadow one by one
      │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_SHADOW_OUTLINE
│     │  │  └─ Skip if font_shadow_color.a == 0 || shadow_outline_size <= 0
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_SHADOW
│     │  │  └─ Skip if font_shadow_color.a == 0
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_STACKED_OUTLINE
│     │  │  └─ Skip if font_stacked_outline_colors/sizes empty
│     │  │  └─ Multiple iterations based on outline stack depth
│     │  │
│     │  ├─ DRAW_STEP_OUTLINE
│     │  │  └─ Skip if outline_size <= 0 || font_outline_color.a == 0
│     │  │
│     │  └─ DRAW_STEP_TEXT
│     │
│     └─ For each drawing step:
│        │
│        ├─ Draw RTL ellipsis (if RTL and has ellipsis)
│        │
│        ├─ Draw main text glyphs (respecting trim positions)
│        │
│        └─ Draw LTR ellipsis (if LTR and has ellipsis)
│
└─ Move to next paragraph
```

Which is far too complicated considering our current implementations without a slight refractor to the rendering loop (as we are doing every render job in a single heavily nested loop).

This [specific commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104731/commits/0fe221022e1abf293435de610d8083f7a047de63) can be controversial, as flattens render loop (for better maintenance clarity).

The reason is that too much branch logic inside one single text line drawing loop complicates the ongoing implementation of stacked drop shadow (and its outline) drawings.

Will gradient outlines be implemented in this pr? I think that would be awesome if we can use built-in settings which is more preferred than shaders + `CanvasGroup`s

> Will gradient outlines be implemented in this pr?

As `Label` does not initially support gradients, I think No. That should be implemented in `RichTextLabel`. Let's see if anyone with better expertise can offer a follow-up PR implementing Gradient-related features in `RichTextLabel` (the source code in RTL is a little too complex for me to read through, but I can try if no one is available).

While the stacked text shadow is capable of covering the function of stacked outline, stacked outline provides better usability, as the outline size is calculated automatically for them, for example, if the user sets outline size to be `[3, 3]`, the actual outline size will be `[3, 6]`, which is more intuitive.

> I think non-overridden items should be empty arrays instead

I will have to look into it, but I think it's Godot's default behavior if I don't implement any specific logic (I merely imitate other implementations).

> There should be a node configuration warning when there's a mismatch between the number of outline/shadow colors and sizes/offsets

Yes, I will try to implement that.

> Changes to colors within constant arrays are not applied instantly ... This may be a more general issue with the array property editors

I will see what I can do about that, but I haven't looked at `EditorPropertyArray` yet. I ended up implementing a dedicated array property inspector for the theme editor.

> I would consider only using LabelSettings instead of theme.

I haven't looked at how `LabelSettings` work yet, but I do agree that the theme is really limited, especially when constructing shadow offsets. Should I take the `LabelSetting` path?
